entries.title: Git worktree (extra checkout of a project)
entries.what: A second working copy of the same git project, checked out on its own branch, next to the main one. Tools like Claude Code create one per parallel session (in .claude/worktrees) so sessions don't step on each other. You can also make them yourself with "git worktree add".
entries.safetyText: The copy's own files are cheap to recreate, but its branch may have work that isn't merged or pushed anywhere. Miu checks this with git before cleaning.
entries.whyBig: Each copy has its own node_modules, build output and caches, so a project that is 15 GB with dependencies costs another 15 GB per worktree.
howTo: Make sure the branch is merged or pushed (Miu shows the branch and whether it's pushed when git is installed).
From the main project folder, remove it with git, which also tidies git's own records.
If you already deleted the folder by hand, run the prune command so git forgets it.
Only want the space back but keep the worktree? Clean its node_modules, build output and caches instead: they're rebuildable.
entries.search: git worktree remove what is a worktree

entries.title: Git repository data (.git)
entries.what: The complete history of a git project: every commit, branch and stash. It's what makes the folder a git repository.
entries.safetyText: Deleting it erases the project's history, branches and any commits that were never pushed. Don't delete it to save space.
entries.whyBig: Projects with big binary files in their history, or many branches, can grow to gigabytes.
howTo: To make it smaller without losing anything, let git compact it.
Large files in history? Use Git LFS or rewrite history only if you know what you're doing.

entries.title: Git LFS objects
entries.what: Large files (images, videos, models) stored by Git Large File Storage, outside the normal history.
entries.safetyText: Old versions can be pruned safely with git lfs; files you still have checked out are kept.
howTo: Run git lfs prune in the project to remove old local copies that are also on the server.

entries.title: node_modules (JavaScript dependencies)
entries.what: The packages a JavaScript or TypeScript project downloaded from npm, pnpm, yarn or bun. They're listed in package.json and the lock file, so they can be reinstalled exactly.
entries.safetyText: Rebuilt by your package manager. Expect a few minutes and a download next time you work on the project.
entries.whyBig: Every project keeps its own copy of every dependency, often 300 MB to several GB, and many small files.
howTo: Remove it (Miu sends it to the Recycle Bin / Trash).
When you come back to the project, reinstall.

entries.title: Next.js build output (.next)
entries.what: Compiled pages, server bundles and the build cache from "next build" or "next dev".
entries.safetyText: Recreated the next time you run the dev server or build.
entries.whyBig: The build cache keeps compiled versions of every page and image.
howTo: Remove it; run next dev or next build again.

entries.title: Nuxt build output (.nuxt / .output)
entries.what: Generated files from a Nuxt app's dev server or build.
entries.safetyText: Recreated automatically.
howTo: Remove it; it comes back on the next dev or build.

entries.title: SvelteKit generated files (.svelte-kit)
entries.what: Types and build output generated by SvelteKit.
entries.safetyText: Recreated automatically.

entries.title: Angular build cache (.angular/cache)
entries.what: Angular CLI's build cache that speeds up rebuilds.
entries.safetyText: Rebuilt on the next build (the first one is slower).

entries.title: Turborepo / Nx cache
entries.what: Cached task results (builds, tests) so monorepo tools can skip work.
entries.safetyText: Only makes the next run slower.

entries.title: Parcel / Vite / ESLint caches
entries.what: Build-tool caches (.parcel-cache, node_modules/.vite, .eslintcache).
entries.safetyText: Rebuilt automatically.

entries.title: Build output (dist / build / out)
entries.what: Files your project's build step produced (bundled JavaScript, compiled code, packaged apps).
entries.safetyText: Usually rebuildable, but some projects keep hand-written files or releases here. Miu only calls it Safe when the project has a build script and git ignores the folder.
howTo: Check it isn't tracked in git (Miu does this).
Remove it and run the build again when needed.

entries.title: Test coverage reports
entries.what: HTML and data files produced by test coverage tools (coverage, .nyc_output, htmlcov).
entries.safetyText: Recreated by running tests with coverage.

entries.title: Python bytecode cache (__pycache__)
entries.what: Compiled .pyc files Python writes next to your code to start faster.
entries.safetyText: Python recreates them automatically.

entries.title: Python virtual environment (.venv / venv / env)
entries.what: A private copy of Python plus the packages a project installed with pip, uv or poetry.
entries.safetyText: Can be recreated from requirements.txt / pyproject.toml. Miu only calls it Safe when it really is a venv (it contains pyvenv.cfg).
entries.whyBig: Data-science packages (torch, tensorflow, CUDA libraries) can be several GB each.
howTo: Remove it.
Recreate it when you need the project again.

entries.title: Python tool caches
entries.what: Caches from pytest, mypy, ruff, tox and similar tools.
entries.safetyText: Rebuilt on the next run.

entries.title: pip / uv download cache
entries.what: Downloaded Python packages kept so reinstalls are fast.
entries.safetyText: Safe to clear; packages are downloaded again when needed.

entries.title: Conda package cache (pkgs)
entries.what: Downloaded conda packages and unpacked copies kept after installs.
entries.safetyText: Let conda remove what no environment uses.
entries.whyBig: Every version of every package you ever installed can stay here.

entries.title: Rust build output (target)
entries.what: Compiled crates and binaries from cargo build / cargo test.
entries.safetyText: Rebuilt by cargo (it can take a while for big projects).
entries.whyBig: Debug and release builds of every dependency, per project: often 2-20 GB.

entries.title: Cargo download cache
entries.what: Crates downloaded by cargo, shared by all your Rust projects.
entries.safetyText: Safe to trim; cargo downloads crates again when needed.

entries.title: Java / Maven build output (target)
entries.what: Compiled classes and packaged jars from Maven.
entries.safetyText: Rebuilt by mvn package.

entries.title: Gradle build output (build / .gradle)
entries.what: Compiled output and the project-local Gradle cache.
entries.safetyText: Rebuilt by Gradle.

entries.title: Gradle global caches (~/.gradle/caches)
entries.what: Downloaded libraries and build caches shared by all Gradle projects.
entries.safetyText: Gradle downloads what it needs again (first builds are slower). Stop Gradle daemons first.
entries.whyBig: Every library version every project ever used.
howTo: Stop running Gradle daemons.
Remove the caches folder.

entries.title: Maven local repository (~/.m2/repository)
entries.what: Every library Maven downloaded for your projects.
entries.safetyText: Re-downloaded when a project needs it (slower first build).

entries.title: .NET build output (bin / obj)
entries.what: Compiled assemblies and intermediate files from dotnet build or Visual Studio.
entries.safetyText: Rebuilt by the next build.

entries.title: NuGet package cache
entries.what: Packages downloaded by dotnet and Visual Studio, shared by all .NET projects.
entries.safetyText: Use dotnet to clear it safely.
entries.whyBig: Every version of every package ever restored.

entries.title: Visual Studio cache (.vs / ipch)
entries.what: Visual Studio's per-solution cache: IntelliSense databases, browse info and settings.
entries.safetyText: Visual Studio rebuilds it (window layout for that solution resets). Close Visual Studio first.

entries.title: Go build cache
entries.what: Compiled packages Go keeps to speed up builds.
entries.safetyText: Safe; use go to clear it.

entries.title: Go module cache (go/pkg/mod)
entries.what: Downloaded Go modules. Files are read-only, so deleting by hand often fails.
entries.safetyText: Use go to clear it (it fixes the read-only permissions).

entries.title: PHP Composer dependencies (vendor)
entries.what: Packages installed by Composer for a PHP project.
entries.safetyText: Reinstalled from composer.lock.

entries.title: Ruby gems (vendor/bundle)
entries.what: Gems installed for a Ruby project.
entries.safetyText: Reinstalled from Gemfile.lock.

entries.title: Dart / Flutter build files (.dart_tool / build)
entries.what: Generated files and build output of a Flutter or Dart project.
entries.safetyText: Rebuilt on the next run.

entries.title: CocoaPods (Pods)
entries.what: iOS/macOS libraries installed by CocoaPods.
entries.safetyText: Reinstalled from Podfile.lock.

entries.title: Xcode DerivedData
entries.what: Build products, indexes and logs Xcode keeps for every project you opened.
entries.safetyText: Xcode rebuilds it (the next build and indexing take longer). Close Xcode first.
entries.whyBig: Old projects you no longer open keep their data here forever.
howTo: Quit Xcode.
Remove the project folders inside DerivedData (or all of it).

entries.title: Xcode device support files
entries.what: Debug symbols copied from each iPhone/iPad/Watch OS version you connected.
entries.safetyText: Safe for OS versions you no longer debug on; Xcode copies them again when you connect such a device.

entries.title: iOS Simulator devices
entries.what: Simulator devices and their apps and data.
entries.safetyText: Let Xcode remove simulators for OS versions you no longer have.

entries.title: Android emulator images (AVD)
entries.what: Virtual Android devices you created in Android Studio, each with its own disk image.
entries.safetyText: Each device's data (installed apps, logins) is lost. Remove unused devices from Android Studio's Device Manager.
entries.whyBig: Each emulator is a full Android system image, often 2-10 GB.
howTo: Open Android Studio › Device Manager.
Delete devices you don't use.

entries.title: Android SDK system images
entries.what: Android versions downloaded for emulators.
entries.safetyText: Remove versions you don't need from the SDK Manager.
howTo: Android Studio › Settings › Android SDK › SDK Platforms: untick old versions.

entries.title: .terraform (Terraform plugins)
entries.what: Provider plugins and modules Terraform downloaded for this configuration.
entries.safetyText: Downloaded again with terraform init.

entries.title: npm / pnpm / yarn / bun cache
entries.what: Shared download caches of JavaScript package managers.
entries.safetyText: Safe to clear with the tool; packages are downloaded again when needed.

entries.title: Playwright / Puppeteer / Cypress browsers
entries.what: Whole browser builds downloaded for automated testing.
entries.safetyText: Downloaded again by the test tool when needed.
entries.whyBig: Each browser version is 150-400 MB, and old versions stay after upgrades.

entries.title: Hugging Face cache
entries.what: AI models and datasets downloaded by transformers, diffusers and other Hugging Face tools.
entries.safetyText: Re-downloadable, but models can be huge to fetch again. Remove the ones you no longer use.
entries.whyBig: A single model can be 5-100 GB.

entries.title: Ollama models
entries.what: Local AI models pulled with ollama.
entries.safetyText: Remove models you don't use with ollama (it also cleans shared layers).

entries.title: LM Studio models
entries.what: AI models downloaded in LM Studio.
entries.safetyText: Delete unused models from LM Studio's My Models screen.

entries.title: Docker Desktop disk image
entries.what: The virtual disk holding all your Docker images, containers, volumes and build cache.
entries.safetyText: Deleting it destroys every container and volume (databases included). Free space from inside Docker instead.
entries.whyBig: Images and build cache pile up with every build; the virtual disk grows but never shrinks on its own.
howTo: See what uses space.
Remove unused images, stopped containers and build cache (Miu's Dev Projects › Docker does this safely).
On Windows/WSL the file doesn't shrink by itself afterwards: compact it.

entries.title: WSL Linux disk (ext4.vhdx)
entries.what: The virtual disk of a Linux distribution installed with WSL: your Linux home folder, packages and files.
entries.safetyText: Deleting it deletes that whole Linux installation. Clean up inside Linux, then compact the disk.
entries.whyBig: It grows as Linux writes files but doesn't shrink when they're deleted.
howTo: Free space inside Linux (apt clean, remove old files).
Shut WSL down, then compact the disk.
